controller.title: An actual protocol peer
controller.description: A pinned prplMesh controller now emits real discovery frames into the isolated EMOSA container network. Its inventory remains empty because EMOSA has not answered or onboarded an extender.
responsibilities: Use the isolated em-protocol bridge, separate from pod management.
Exercise discovery, capabilities and selected provisioning procedures.
Retain captures from an independent bridge observation point.
controller.next: Use the recorded peer build for actual EMOSA discovery/WSC after P0. Configure its BSS policy first and resolve the recorded native shutdown aborts before recovery qualification.

agent.title: The extender’s EasyMesh representation
agent.description: EMOSA represents an unchanged OpenSync extender as an agent that a real EasyMesh controller can discover and onboard. The agent endpoint runs around the controller; the extender keeps OpenSync.
responsibilities: Map stable agent/radio/BSS identities and advertised capabilities to a qualified actual pod.
Bound framing, TLVs, reassembly, retries and timers using the selected specifications.
Authenticate and validate genuine WSC provisioning.
Bind the complete radio BSS request to supported semantic operations.
agent.next: M1 construction and M2 payload authentication now have independent hostap fixtures. Complete IEEE framing, controller/radio binding, exchange state and complete-radio mapping before any wire-driven pod operation.

engine.title: Intent becomes an observable operation
engine.description: The operation engine separates desired configuration, an acknowledged database commit, and fresh observed application.
responsibilities: Serialize modifications per pod and reject excess requests.
Guard existing resource references and preserve unrelated configuration.
Reconcile lost outcomes, restart, ownership conflicts and deadlines.
engine.next: Bind this tested semantic path to genuine provisioning; keep client behavior as a separate observation boundary.

journal.title: Recovery has a durable record
journal.description: SQLite stores operation transitions, attempts, observations and events so recovery does not depend on a surviving process.
responsibilities: Use scoped idempotency and a single-writer process lock.
Persist secret references and keyed fingerprints; keep credentials in private files.
Preserve unknown attribution and deadline failures when evidence arrives late.
journal.next: Verify the same recovery semantics when a physical pod carries its own management connection.

ovsdb.title: The existing management boundary
ovsdb.description: The adapter uses the upstream OVS client with bounded sessions, monitor caches and guarded transactions.
responsibilities: Read the actual schema, radio/VIF references and supported security representation.
Patch only fields covered by a qualified mapping.
Resynchronize after reconnect before accepting new writes.
ovsdb.next: Use read-only qualification to replace synthetic mapping assumptions with actual pod evidence. The pinned OpenSync schema is only an upstream simulation reference.

pod.title: Keep the physical pod unchanged
pod.description: The pod keeps its firmware and managers. EMOSA uses its existing authorized OVSDB management interface; it installs no software on the pod.
responsibilities: Identify the actual model, firmware, schema and radio/VIF inventory.
Verify writer control, endpoint trust and a recoverable management path.
Qualify a sole-BSS radio or the complete radio-wide provisioning scope.
pod.next: Collect a read-only draft, verify remaining M0 checks, and run a wire-driven change on a named target after I4.

client.title: Observe what a station experiences
client.status: hwsim smoke passed · physical client pending
client.description: A wpa_supplicant station in an LXD container can observe authentication and traffic independently of the adapter’s database view.
responsibilities: Use mac80211_hwsim for a simulated AP/station lab.
Use a real Wi-Fi interface for a physical pod; hwsim has no RF link to hardware.
Record BSSID/SSID, association, authentication, reachability and reconnect timing.
client.next: Integrate a separate Config-to-hostapd manager with independently observed State, then use a physical Wi-Fi client for the actual unchanged-pod demonstration.

evaluator.title: Evidence connects the boundaries
evaluator.description: The evaluator runs scenarios, injects bounded faults and retains inspectable results. This site reads a curated published snapshot.
responsibilities: Keep immutable inputs, source hashes, operation timelines and observations.
Compare successes, failures and blocked experiments without changing their verdicts.
Add independent packet and client artifacts when those boundaries are available.
evaluator.next: Deliver one reproducible end-to-end evidence bundle and repeat it with an independent controller.

model.title: Exercise the operation contract
model.description: Start here for deterministic recovery, deadline, conflict and multi-pod experiments without privileged resources.
model.path: Semantic scenario → operation engine → deterministic model
model.proves: Operation transitions, idempotency, serialization, recovery rules and truthful deadline outcomes.
model.limits: No real OVSDB protocol, EasyMesh exchange, radio or physical pod is exercised.
model.prerequisites: The repository, uv and pinned CPython 3.13.7. No LXD or radio is required.
model.command:
uv sync --frozen
uv run pytest -m unit
uv run emosa-lab run scenarios/component-bss-change.json --backend model
model.note: Use the returned run ID with emosa-lab report, watch or inspect. Local evidence is written under .lab/runs/.

ovsdb.title: Cross the real database boundary
ovsdb.description: Use a real ovsdb-server with the pinned OpenSync schema and a separate manager simulator. Only that manager writes simulated State.
ovsdb.path: Semantic scenario → EMOSA → real OVSDB → simulated manager → observed State
ovsdb.proves: Schema/monitor handling, guarded Config edits, independent simulated application and lost-reply reconciliation.
ovsdb.limits: The initiating request is semantic. There are no EasyMesh packets, Linux Wi-Fi association or physical device claims.
ovsdb.prerequisites: Locked Python environment plus a C compiler, make, libc headers and pkg-config for the isolated OVSDB build.
ovsdb.command:
bash scripts/build-ovsdb.sh
uv run pytest -m ovsdb
uv run emosa-lab run scenarios/component-bss-change.json --backend ovsdb-sim
uv run emosa-lab run scenarios/component-lost-reply.json --backend ovsdb-sim
ovsdb.note: The upstream plume-design/opensync schema is pinned at 78d8a7194d5e77635877cc456231e7be5cf03d68. It is not a qualified profile of any actual pod.

hwsim.title: Add a simulated 802.11 link
hwsim.status: Standalone radio smoke passed · EMOSA binding pending
hwsim.description: Two mac80211_hwsim radios live in the dedicated lab VM’s kernel. One is assigned to an AP container running hostapd, the other to a station container running wpa_supplicant.
hwsim.path: em-radio-ap / hostapd ⇄ mac80211_hwsim virtual medium ⇄ em-radio-client / wpa_supplicant
hwsim.proves: Executed in the dedicated Ubuntu/LXD VM: WPA2-PSK association, three successful interface-bound pings, and a virtual-medium capture. Clean setup and retest passed.
hwsim.limits: The harness is separate from the current OVSDB manager simulator. Its radio smoke test cannot prove EMOSA actuation, EasyMesh provisioning, RF behavior or real-pod compatibility.
hwsim.prerequisites: A dedicated emosa-lab VM, initialized inner LXD, pinned Ubuntu image, available hwsim module and documented VM/container packages. See the full procedure before setup.
hwsim.command:
# Inside the dedicated emosa-lab VM
python3 deploy/hwsim/lab.py check
sudo python3 deploy/hwsim/lab.py setup
sudo python3 deploy/hwsim/lab.py smoke
# Remove only resources created by this harness
sudo python3 deploy/hwsim/lab.py cleanup
hwsim.note: The retained smoke passed with no setup Ethernet interface. This is a working AP/station harness; a manager-to-hostapd binding and controller discovery/onboarding remain separate implementation gates.

physical.title: Qualify the unchanged target first
physical.description: Collect actual pod facts using local secret references. The output is always a draft and never automatically enables writes.
physical.path: Real EasyMesh → EMOSA → unchanged pod → physical Wi-Fi station → independent observation
physical.proves: Read-only collection establishes available schema and inventory facts. Later wire-driven hardware runs establish behavior only for the named pod/build and procedure.
physical.limits: A schema match alone does not qualify mappings, writer ownership, recovery or radio-wide WSC behavior. hwsim cannot associate with a physical pod.
physical.prerequisites: Trusted endpoint and credentials in private local files; actual model/build, radio/VIF scope, verified cloud-writer control, recovery path and an independent client with a real Wi-Fi interface.
physical.command:
# Create the private connection file per docs/pod-qualification.md
# The output directory must not already exist.
uv run emosa qualify-pod \
  --connection /home/rev/.config/emosa/pods/pod-1/connection.json \
  --output /home/rev/.local/state/emosa/qualification/pod-1-first-read
physical.note: The first actuation experiment should use wired management and one qualified sole-BSS radio. Test lost replies and restart before progressing to wireless management and an independent controller.

run_catalog.label: Baseline BSS change
run_catalog.annotation: A direct semantic change was committed through real OVSDB and observed after application by a separate simulated manager.

run_catalog.label: Lost reply & recovery
run_catalog.annotation: The desired state was observed after resynchronization. The missing reply leaves commit attribution unknown; the run does not invent an acknowledgement.

run_catalog.label: Apply deadline exceeded
run_catalog.annotation: A deliberately short 0.01-second deadline failed. Later observation did not change the original failure into a pass.

run_catalog.label: Genuine provisioning gate
run_catalog.annotation: The scenario required a genuine EasyMesh exchange. P0 prerequisites were absent, so the run blocked without a semantic fallback.

run_catalog.label: Server restart · earlier failure
run_catalog.annotation: An earlier build exposed a simulator-manager reconnect problem. Its failure remains in the retained evidence.

run_catalog.label: Server restart · corrected retest
run_catalog.annotation: The simulated manager lifecycle now follows a simulated pod/server restart. This later build passed the component recovery expectation.

roadmap.title: Freeze the protocol contract
roadmap.description: Review the proposed IEEE 1905.1-2013 + 1905.1a-2014, EasyMesh 6.1 and WPS 2.0.10 corpus. Obtain missing IEEE text, select the initial procedure scope and finish the normative rule matrix.
roadmap.evidence: Selected editions, rule/section references, complete radio-scope rules and independently checked packet/crypto vectors.

roadmap.title: Discover and onboard the represented extender
roadmap.description: Select a real EasyMesh controller/build early. Implement the adapter’s virtual-agent discovery, qualified capabilities and genuine WSC onboarding/provisioning. First exercise actual frames against OVSDB simulation.
roadmap.evidence: Controller agent/topology view plus independent captures showing discovery, identity and onboarding; valid/invalid provisioning; duplicate/retry and lost-reply behavior.
roadmap.action: Follow I3 and I4 exit conditions

roadmap.title: Qualify the physical pod and observer
roadmap.description: Supply trusted local connection inputs for read-only collection. Verify actual schema, firmware, a sole-BSS radio or complete BSS scope, writer controls, wired recovery and a real Wi-Fi client.
roadmap.evidence: A reviewed target profile with concrete observations for every required field; no automatic promotion from a draft.
roadmap.action: Collect and review the draft profile

roadmap.title: Show the OpenSync extender as an EasyMesh agent
roadmap.description: Have the controller discover and onboard the EMOSA agent backed by one unchanged OpenSync extender. Apply a supported BSS change through the adapter and verify it with an independent physical client.
roadmap.evidence: Controller inventory before/after onboarding, stable identity and qualified capabilities, real frames, Config/State changes, physical client traffic and recovery. Record interventions.

roadmap.title: Make the result reproducible and independent
roadmap.description: Retain the Ubuntu/LXD image and package manifests, qualify wireless management separately, and repeat the procedure with a named independent EasyMesh controller. Use hwsim for useful client-stack tests along the way.
roadmap.evidence: A clean-environment rerun plus an independent-peer result for the declared procedure and versions. Optional native OpenSync work does not gate a ready physical experiment.
